title: UK police say 325 people were arrested at Palestine Action demo
gist: London's Metropolitan Police arrested 325 people at a Palestine Action support demonstration outside the US embassy, 320 for expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act, ahead of a UK Supreme Court hearing on the July 2025 ban. Campaigners and police tallies put total arrests since the ban at over 4,000, and the US also designated the group terrorist in August.

themes.theme: Mass arrests under UK terror law

insights.claim: London's Metropolitan Police arrested 325 people at a Palestine Action support protest outside the US embassy, 320 of them for expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Scale of enforcement highlights escalating civil-liberties tensions in UK protest policing.
insights.quote: The vast majority of arrests -- 320 -- were for expressing support for a proscribed organisation under the Terrorism Act.

insights.claim: More than 4,000 people, including many senior citizens and Holocaust survivors, have been arrested for showing support for Palestine Action since its proscription, according to campaigners and police tallies.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Sustained mass arrests signal a durable domestic political flashpoint for the UK government.

insights.claim: Support for or membership of Palestine Action is a crime punishable by up to 14 years in prison under the UK designation, which places it on the same blacklist as Hamas.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Severe penalties raise the legal and reputational stakes of the Supreme Court challenge.

insights.claim: Police Scotland made no arrests at a smaller Edinburgh protest outside the US consulate but said enquiries are ongoing and further action will be taken as appropriate.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Follow-up enforcement implies the crackdown extends beyond London.
insights.quote: Evidence is being reviewed and further action will be taken as appropriate.
insights.locator: Evidence is being reviewed and further

insights.claim: The UK Supreme Court is holding a two-day hearing on the government's July 2025 decision to outlaw Palestine Action under anti-terror legislation.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A ruling against the ban would be a significant check on executive use of terror laws against protest groups.

insights.claim: The United States designated Palestine Action as terrorist in August as the Trump administration intensifies its campaign against left-wing movements.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: US-UK alignment on designations points to broader Western tightening against activist networks.
